purpose: Documents full-text editorial review of newly downloaded posts before canonical ingestion.

posts.title: The Moral Benefits of Capitalism
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Argues that broadly shared economic growth under capitalism can promote moral progress by reducing poverty and fostering opportunity, tolerance, and social mobility, while stagnation and extreme inequality produce the opposite effects.

posts.title: Is Capitalism Anti-Christian?
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Reconsiders whether capitalism is inherently anti-Christian, arguing that Jesus could not have opposed a modern economic system and that his moral teachings bear more directly on how people behave within it.

posts.title: September 2026 Gold Q&A
posts.author: jennao
posts.description: Announces the September 2026 Gold and Platinum member Q&A and provides details for submitting questions and joining the live Zoom session.

posts.title: Martyrs, Forgers, and Textual Scholars:  Intriguing Questions From Readers
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Answers reader questions about miraculous portrayals of Christian martyrs, whether ancient secretaries can explain the authorship of the Pastoral Epistles, and the likely future of New Testament textual criticism.

posts.title: Flipping a Coin. Cephas and Peter: One Person or Two?
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Reconsiders the argument that Peter and Cephas were different early Christians, weighing Pauline evidence and early tradition against the difficulty that both men would have borne versions of the same previously unknown nickname.

posts.title: Other Suggestions That Peter and Cephas Were Two Different People
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Argues from Paul's wording in 1 Corinthians 15 that Cephas may have been a convert who received a resurrection appearance rather than Peter, one of Jesus' Twelve.
